title: Rational equivalence on a product with the projective line: the two fibres of an integral closed subscheme and the generation of rationally trivial cycles
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the technical engine behind the identification of rational equivalence with the relations coming from the projective line: it shows that for an integral W in the product of X with the projective line, not equal to either standard fibre, the two fibres are effective Cartier divisors that can be viewed in X and are rationally equivalent, that the same holds for a locally finite family, and conversely that every rationally trivial cycle arises this way (statement lines 3334-3360, tag 02S4). The proof combines the pullback criterion for effective Cartier divisors, the properness of the projection, the graph construction attached to a rational function and the proper pushforward statement for rational equivalence, and the last part requires building the W_i from the rational functions realising the triviality of alpha. That construction is the substance, so the claim is H2.
